Let
\[
\pi:C_\lambda\to \mathbb P^1_x
\]
be the natural map. For \(\lambda\ne 0,1\), the branch points are \(0,1,\lambda,\infty\).

For \(\lambda\ne1\), the two Kummer classes \(x(x-1)\) and \(x(x-\lambda)\) are independent, since their divisors have simple zeros at different points \(1\) and \(\lambda\). Hence
\[
[\mathbb C(C_\lambda):\mathbb C(x)]=mn.
\]
The ramification indices over the four branch points are:
\[
e_0=\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=\ell,\qquad e_1=m,\qquad e_\lambda=n,
\]
and, since both functions have pole order \(2\) at infinity,
\[
e_\infty=\operatorname{lcm}\left(\frac m{\gcd(m,2)},\frac n{\gcd(n,2)}\right)=\frac{\ell}{h}.
\]
Riemann-Hurwitz gives
\[
2g(C_\lambda)-2
=mn\left(-2+\left(1-\frac1\ell\right)+\left(1-\frac1m\right)+\left(1-\frac1n\right)+\left(1-\frac h\ell\right)\right),
\]
so
\[
g(C_\lambda)=1+\frac{mn}{2}\left(2-\frac1m-\frac1n-\frac{1+h}{\ell}\right).
\]

When \(\lambda=1\), the field is
\[
\mathbb C(x)(y,z)=\mathbb C(x)(u),\qquad u^\ell=x(x-1),
\]
so the cover has degree \(\ell\). Its ramification indices over \(0,1,\infty\) are
\[
\ell,\quad \ell,\quad \frac{\ell}{h}.
\]
Thus
\[
2g(C_1)-2
=\ell\left(-2+2\left(1-\frac1\ell\right)+\left(1-\frac h\ell\right)\right)
=\ell-2-h,
\]
hence
\[
g(C_1)=\frac{\ell-h}{2}.
\]

Therefore the genus drop is
\[
\boxed{\Delta_{m,n}
=\frac{2+2mn-m-n-\ell-d(1+h)+h}{2}}.
\]
